label: Multi-horizon forecasting from an origin snapshot
summary: A runnable reference for forecasting many series at several horizons with origin-safe features, quantile boosting, forecast value added against a seasonal baseline, censored demand and late feeds.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 15 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 300 series by 730 days with about 2.5% constrained days. baseline.py reports WMAPE about 0.12 for the model against 0.20-0.22 for the seasonal baseline (forecast value added 0.43 at horizons 1, 3 and 7 and 0.36 at 14), P90 coverage near 0.89, aggregate WMAPE 0.026 against 0.123 at series level, and 0.198 against 0.141 when a late feed is read as zero instead of missing. pytest reports 8 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic series with seasonality, promotions, shocks, a leading indicator and capped (censored) days
Origin-safe features per series, origin and horizon, including late-feed handling
Origin-based split, seasonal baseline, P50 and P90 boosting, forecast value added, coverage and the late-feed experiment
Executable gates: determinism, origin safety, late feeds, split order, value added, coverage and the aggregate trap

synthetic.description: 300 series over 730 days with weekly and annual seasonality, trend, planned promotions, shared external shocks, a 14-day leading indicator, noise of about 18%, and capped days (2.5%) where the observed value understates demand.
knobs: n_series, days: number of series and history length (defaults 300 and 730)
seed: identical seed gives an identical table
constants in the file: promotion uplift, shock sensitivity, leading-indicator share by horizon, censoring depth

slots.meaning: mean of the last 7 and 28 days and their ratio, known at the forecast origin
values on the same weekday in previous weeks
what is already booked or ordered for the target day at the origin
promotion and external-signal flags for the target day, as published at the origin
how many of the recent days are missing in the feed

data.threshold: pytest -k 'deterministic or precede' passes; the leading indicator correlates above 0.5 with next-day demand
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Corrupting every value after the origin (set to 1,000,000) changes no feature; a late day counts as missing_7 = 1, not as zero

baseline.threshold: Recorded per horizon at series level and in aggregate (the kit's seasonal baseline has WMAPE 0.20-0.22)

challenger.metric: Forecast value added and band coverage
challenger.threshold: At least 0.25 at every horizon and P90 coverage between 85% and 95% (the kit reaches 0.36-0.43 and 89%)

tests.pass: Setting every value after the origin to 1,000,000 changes no feature
A missing latest day is counted and does not pull the recent mean down

tests.test: Forecast value added and band coverage
tests.pass: At least 0.25 at horizons 1, 3, 7 and 14 and P90 coverage between 85% and 95%
Aggregate WMAPE is below half the series-level WMAPE
WMAPE with the day left missing is below 85% of WMAPE with the day zero-filled

lessons.trap: Reading a late feed as zero
lessons.evidence: With the newest day missing for every series, zero-filling gives WMAPE 0.198 and leaving it missing gives 0.141 (0.123 with a complete feed).
On the 2.3% of capped days the observed values were 44% of the demand the model expected, so those days are excluded from training and scoring.
WMAPE 0.12 sounds good until the seasonal baseline turns out to be 0.20 on the same data; forecast value added is 0.43 at short horizons.
The same forecasts score WMAPE 0.026 in aggregate but 0.123 at series level, about a fifth.

target: The target is the observed value on day t+h divided by the series' recent average at forecast origin t, so one model serves every series. Capped days are excluded.
